x: Archie Bedford ran a good race to beat Pudicombe of S.L.H. in the 2 miles, with Eric Herbert in third place, and the final points position was :—Belgrave H., 33; South London H., 16; Leicester, 5. In the junior match we had Ian Forrester winning the 100, with Frank Kemp taking the 220 and P.

Our team duly qualified by finishing second to Herne Hill in the heat and then in the final they gained third-place medals, with South London just beating Herne Hill for first place. In the junior medley relay we saw P.
Frank Kemp was second in the Junior 100 yards, but won the 220 in 22.8 seconds, which is some going for a junior. P.
Frank Kemp scored a double win in the 100 and 220 yards, and Ian Forrester won the second string race in the latter event. P.
Schools 1 Mile Race in 4 min. 28.2 secs., and P.
At Broomfield Park, on July 7th, our only success was in the 440 yards, in which P.

Maclean jumped for us in the High Jump and Gordon Lowers turned out in the Long Jump and Javelin events. We fared much better in the junior match, with Frank Kemp having a dual sprint victory, as did P.
The holder, Denis Merrett, was unable to run owing to injury. Frank Kemp retained his 100 yards junior title with P.
Jim Heathfield was second, a position he usually occupies in Club championship races over this distance, and Alan Bishop was third. Peter Casselton retained his 440 junior title with J.

Quite a number of our lads are now having to join up to do their National Service training and recent joinings include—Peter Casselton to the R.A., Charlie Henn to the R.E.M.E., Peter Courtney who managed to get placed in the half and mile at his Depot Sports.
440 yards · P. J. Casselton · July, 1951 · 51.4 secs.
Peter Casselton, our Junior 440 yds. champion, is now in Germany with the B.A.O.R., and ran in the championships out there, but found that Army life is not good training for running.

After the first two laps, their nomination Peter Casselton, began to prove them right. Although at one time it looked as if Patterson was going to upset the odds, Casselton's strength and speed stood him in good stead.
Pete Casselton although qualifying for the final of the Senior 440 yards with a second in his heat in 58.1 secs. could not show an improvement in the final.
